summary: The wizard kills a Keystone Kop through the natural #wizkill command path. C reaches mon.c:mondead and draws rnd(5)=4 after the death count, then removes the corpse and leaves a corpse glyph. JavaScript stops at the unported Kop return arm, uses no source-matched draw, and leaves the Kop glyph. The whole mondead function also contains source-required pet-sadness, steam-vortex cloud, and vault-guard branches currently refused in JavaScript. The guard branch consumes vault.c:grddead's boolean result; grddead requires clear_fcorr and parkguard, and mongone is its second mondead-family caller.

source.branch: mon.c:mondead() (3081-3177) clears iflags.sad_feeling, applies lifesaving and vampire reversion, prints the pending sad-pet message, creates a harmless cloud for steam-vortex death, and calls vault.c:grddead() for an isgd monster before restoring form, counting deaths, logging, unmapping, and detaching. A Keystone Kop then finds the down staircase and draws rnd(5): case 1 attempts makemon at the staircase and falls through to random placement only without a stair; case 2 calls makemon at (0,0); other values do not respawn. The makemon return is discarded.
callers: The selected natural route is cmd.c:#wizkill -> wizcmds.c:wiz_kill -> mon.c:xkilled -> mon.c:mondead. JavaScript wires cmd.js:runKillCommand -> wizcmds.js:wiz_kill -> mon.js:xkilled -> mon.js:mondead; the admitted case reaches the copied function from this path.

Other direct C mondead callers are mon.c:minliquid_core, mondied, monstone, monkilled, xkilled, kill_genocided_monsters; muse.c:mon_consume; explode.c:mon_explodes; mhitm.c:mon_explodes; and mhitu.c:gazeu. Their existing JavaScript adapters already call mon.js:mondead; this task changes the common source body rather than replacing those adapters.

C mondead and mongone both consume grddead's boolean result and return without detaching when it is false. The JavaScript mondead and mongone guard branches await the canonical vault.js implementation and preserve that early return.

vault.c:grddead calls clear_fcorr(grd, TRUE), and when its result is false it sets hp to zero, parks the guard at (0,0), and calls clear_fcorr again before returning whether the guard can be detached. vault.c:clear_fcorr also serves restfakecorr(); its JavaScript restfakecorr path already awaits the same helper. C gd_move has separate direct clear_fcorr calls in its currently unsupported hostile-guard routes; js/vault.js:gd_move refuses those routes before the matching adapter, and this task does not claim those independent gd_move branches.

grddead's C relobj(grd, 0, FALSE) result is discarded. After accepted A2 Main 043ba3ff2e1b7558f7e25ef1a9daa70130c173f6, vault.js awaits the implemented steal.js:relobj for its gold removal and remaining inventory drops; no return value is consumed.
dependencies: vault.c:clear_fcorr returns a boolean consumed by grddead and restfakecorr; js/vault.js ports its source yelp, stopprint, corridor, and terrain restoration behavior.
vault.c:parkguard is the void helper used by grddead after failed corridor clearing; js/vault.js ports the polearm reference, map removal, parking, and saved coordinates.
vault.c:in_fcorridor is the pure predicate used by clear_fcorr; scripts/vault-guard-escort.test.mjs pins the C half-open fake-corridor loop bounds.
mondead's steam-vortex arm needs region.c:create_gas_cloud, already implemented in js/region.js.

mondead's Kop return arm needs stairs.c:stairway_find_type_dir and makemon.c:makemon; the JavaScript stair finder and makemon_runtime accept these existing call shapes, so no new source ownership is claimed for them.

steal.c:relobj is an accepted A2 dependency, not source ownership in this task. Its implemented findgold, object extraction, obfree, mdrop_obj, and floor effects cover the discarded-void C call from grddead.

The full source comparison of mon.c:mondead() at lines 3081-3177 finds four JavaScript refusals before detach: the sad-feeling message, steam-vortex cloud, vault-guard grddead call, and Keystone Kop resurrection. Existing scripts/mon-kill.test.mjs still asserts refusals for vault-guard and Kop deaths and must be changed to source-pinned behavior. The C source call order puts sad message and gas cloud before guard handling, increments mvitals[].died before the Kop rnd(5), and logs/unmaps/detaches only after the source-specific arms.

The vault dependency trace spans vault.c:clear_fcorr() lines 48-116, parkguard() lines 155-171, grddead() lines 175-188, in_fcorridor() lines 192-201, and mon.c:mongone() lines 3267-3283. grddead consumes clear_fcorr's return twice and calls parkguard between failed attempts; clear_fcorr consumes in_fcorridor's boolean and advances over fakecorr[fcbeg..fcend). Its relobj return is discarded. The JavaScript paths now use the complete vault helpers and accepted steal.js:relobj dependency.

Fresh C/JavaScript comparisons now pass for the selected v43 Kop case (2,086 RNG values and 38 screens/cursors), the independent Kop kill recording (1,913 RNG values and 39 screens/cursors), the natural vault guard-death recording (6,230 RNG values and 162 screens/cursors), and the existing guard-cleanup recording (13,878 RNG values and 304 screens/cursors). These routes exercise mondead, mongone, grddead, clear_fcorr, and parkguard through production callers; in_fcorridor is pinned by a source-based pure-function test.
